-- True when the path, with "." and ".." resolved lexically, stays inside its root.
-- Empty, absolute, and escaping paths are not inside.
inside(path: str) -> bool =
  ex inside("a.txt") == True
  ex inside("sub/../a.txt") == True
  ex inside("..") == False
  ex inside("/etc/passwd") == False
  ex inside("sub/../../x") == False
  if path.char_count() == 0
    return False
  let parts = path.split("/")
  if parts[0].char_count() == 0
    return False
  var depth = 0
  for part in parts
    if part == "" or part == "."
      continue
    if part == ".."
      depth -= 1
      if depth < 0
        return False
      continue
    depth += 1
  True

-- Text of the file `path` under the directory `notes`, or "" if the path
-- escapes `notes`, or the file is missing or unreadable.
read_public(path: str) -> str uses fs =
  ex read_public("..") == ""
  ex read_public("/etc/passwd") == ""
  ex read_public("sub/../../x") == ""
  if not inside(path)
    return ""
  var text = ""
  with fs = fs.sub("notes")
    text = fs.read(path) else ""
  text

test_inside() =
  assert inside("sub/../a.txt")
  assert not inside("..")
  assert not inside("/etc/passwd")
  assert not inside("sub/../../x")

test_read_public_escape() uses fs =
  assert read_public("../secret") == ""
  assert read_public("/etc/passwd") == ""
